description.en:
Operator Pallas has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude for rallying her fellow Minoan operators.
The Field Operations Department has thus passed the following resolution:
This operator shall be appointed a Guard Operator during field operations to exercise Instructor responsibilities.
In witness whereof,
This badge is hereby conferred upon the above named.
description.zh:
干员帕拉斯擅长鼓舞米诺斯出身的干员
根据外勤部门决议
在外勤任务中划分为近卫干员，行使教官职责
特别颁发此证章
以兹证明

description.en:
Because of these black rocks on my body, I had no choice but to leave my homeland, the place where my ancestors defended generations after generations.
It may have caused lots of pain and suffering, but, looking back, I cannot help but smile.
That said, how am I supposed to live when I have to cut all my ties with Minos and abandon my roots?
I would yet like another taste of the herb cakes from Athenius.
I wish to enjoy the fine wine from Lachedamon.
I want to be able to bring home souvenirs from the Lachedamon markets again.
I hope I'll yet be able to lay my heart bare to the scholars, spar with the warriors, and negotiate with the merchants there.
I wonder when I will get to enjoy my life so once again?
Mountains of Minos, please allow me to continue my ramblings.
O Almighty Athos, do you nurture your faithful children of Minos still?
I but wish that those faithful believers who drink your springwater yet give to you their praises and offerings.
Hymnoi, my most respected teacher. Are there still those who seek the meaning of life from your embrace?
I know you keep to yourself, but if those who seek your help are true to heart, I ask you to please guide them to the right path.
O Helia, respected and majestic Helia. Are there yet simpletons who attempt to make their way to your summit merely for fame?
Please, let them return home safely after your punishments. They are young and immature. Please do not take away their future for your brief moments of fury.
The lands of Minos. Words cannot describe how beautiful you are, and nothing comes close to your magnificence.
Yet I must say these words and mark them down for prosperity.
These are only words that a Forte, far away from home, still has for comfort. Should these words go unsaid, these woes deep in my heart will endanger even my life.
Please forgive me for resorting to such shallow methods to compose myself.
I will yet wander outside your domain.
It may take several years, perhaps decades.
But I promise you this.
It matters not how long.
I will once again return to your embrace.
This is the truest, most sincere oath that a Minoan can take.
I am certain you can hear me.
This rock, mined in Aegean, yet remains affixed to my hammer.
With it, I will make it through all obstacles in life.
It will bear witness to my faith, hear my odes, and execute these great deeds with me.
After countless trials and tribulations, the melodies of my return shall be sounded.
At that moment in time, it will recant to you these writings of mine at the temple.
I will ever hold out hope that this day will be soon.
—Excerpts from some disorganized scribblings written by Pallas.
description.zh:
由着这宿于身上的黑石，我终究离开了先祖们代代护佑的故土。
呵，它予我的痛苦，我将报之以微笑。
可是，离了与米诺斯的系绊，失去根源的我又该如何生存？
还想来上一块雅赛努斯的青草饼，
豪饮拉刻代蒙的美酒，
从科林尼亚的市集上买些纪念品带回家。
仍盼望与哲人交心，与武人切磋，与商人谈价。
我要到何时才能重享这样的生活？
米诺斯的诸山啊，还请多听我几句唠叨。
尊贵的阿苏斯，您还在哺育米诺斯的人民吗？
但愿啜饮泉水的信徒们还愿向您奉上赞美与祭品。
荷谟伊，我最敬重的导师，还有人愿意在您怀中领悟生命的真谛吗？
我知道您不擅表达，但若来者满怀真诚，还是请您多多开导他们。
哦，赫里亚，可敬的赫里亚，巍峨的赫里亚，此时此刻，仍有愚者试图攀上您的巅峰以逞一时英雄吗？
给上一些惩罚，然后让他们下山吧，这些人只是年少轻狂，请别因一时之怒夺了他们的未来。
米诺斯的大地啊，言辞于您是多么苍白，任何修饰都及不上您真正的壮丽。
但我还是要说，仍旧要写。
这是远离家乡的丰蹄仅剩下的慰藉，不说不写，心中的病苦就要危及生命。
还请您体谅我，让我用这浅陋的方式平复心情。
我还将在您的疆域外游荡徘徊。
或许数年，或许数十年。
但我仍愿与您约定。
无论岁月几何。
我终将回到您的怀抱。
一位米诺斯人最诚挚的誓言，莫过于此。
我坚信您能听到。
只因一方自爱琴采来的坚石正紧紧嵌在我的锤上。
同我披荆斩棘，与我出生入死。
见证我的信仰、听闻我的诗颂、经手我的伟业。
于万千试炼后，奏响凯旋的旋律。
是时，它将在神殿台柱上，为您讲述我的篇章。
我真诚企盼，彼时彼刻，快快到来。
——摘自帕拉斯笔记上杂乱无序的文字

description.en:
(In the background, desert hills, and the black curtains left over from last year's festival. Hang up two moons.)
(Enter choir from stage left. Chant. Enter the HERO from backstage.)
HERO: My dearest companions! Tonight, in this place, we finally gather.
HERO: We rest our feet on the highest peak of Minos. We stand here and gaze as far as the eye may see, to the land covered by the radiance of the moons. All is our home.
The mountain spring flows forth from here, crosses untold hills, sweeps untold grasslands, and finally flows into the lake of the Aegean Plains, to become one with the blood of us all.
We owe it to our shared language, our shared folksong, our shared beliefs, that we stand here, to expel our common enemy. After tonight, so too will our blood unite.
HERO: Let us drink together from a ladle of this spring water, and as we return in victory, we may then drink together from the mead this spring water creates.
(The HERO, together with every FOLLOWER, imbibes wine. Timmy is still not of age. Please give him ginger ale instead.)
HERO: I imagine we all, when we were born of this land and first opened our eyes, saw that our soil was ravaged by lowly intruders, and that our first wail was mingled with the invaders' satisfied jeers.
We have never seen the great and peaceful days spoken of in the epics, but we've no iota of doubt that this land we call Minos was of much different impression a century ago.
(Performers begin to play here, growing gradually impassioned as the lyrics progress.)
(Choir dances, and pairs off with Originium Arts.)
HERO: Beneath the warm sunshine, the people contested in military fashion, yet did not endanger their lives, but simply tempered their wills and physiques; the crossing of words was not for epithets of hate, but for the pursuit of this land's deepest secrets.
The forests were not places to lay treacherous ambush, for Heria's thickets were of a different image in the verses; the rivers served as more than a channel to break the enemy front, for in them we could bathe and sing loud.
HERO: The rose has need of the thorn's protection, and the beauty of our poems likewise ask for blade and shield to guard them. And we can use their petals to adorn our armor, and see their verses meld with our songs of war.
HERO: Behold, for the moons are at their peak. Our victory in this war is as clear as this night sky. I believe it.
(Turn lighting up to maximum.)
HERO: Warriors, heroes, sharpen your weapons for the very last time.
The withered trees will turn to nourishment that feeds this land, and the ruins of the wild will become as foundations for our rebuilt splendor.
Tonight, we take back our faith, and we take back both the history and future of Minos.
(The HERO raises their sword, and all FOLLOWERS pick up their weapons and line up. Choir chants. Curtains.)
(Pay attention to number of weapons when inventorying props. DO NOT let real weapons get mixed in.)
—From the third act of the Theater of Akroti's 'Light of Heria'. Pallas performs as the HERO CYPHUS, with a great deal of annotations and notes beside each of her lines.
description.zh:
（背景荒山，以及去年狂欢节剩下的黑色幕布，悬挂两个月亮）
（歌队从左侧入，歌唱，英雄从幕后登场）
英雄：我至亲的同袍们，今夜，我们终于会聚于此。
英雄：我们脚下的山峰，是米诺斯的第一高峰。当我们站在此处极目远望，双月的光辉覆盖的地方，都是我们的家乡。
山泉从这里发源，跨越三千里的山地，行过三千里的草原，最终流入爱琴平原的湖泊，融入我们每个人的血液。
是同一种语言，同一首乡谣，同一种信仰，让我们站在这里，驱逐共同的敌人。今夜之后，我们的血也会交汇一处。
英雄：让我们同饮一瓢泉水吧，得胜归来时，我们可以再同饮这泉水酿成的蜜酒。
（英雄和众追随者饮酒，小提米还未成年，请替换成姜汁汽水）
英雄：我想我们每个人都一样，我们自降生在这片土地上，第一次睁开眼，看到的便是遭卑鄙的入侵者摧残过的土地，我们发出的第一声啼哭是和侵略者得意的笑声混在一起的。
虽然我们都不曾见过典籍里描绘的那段诗一般安宁祥和的日子，但我丝毫不怀疑，名为米诺斯的土地在百年前是另一副模样。
（乐手在此处开始奏乐，由抒情逐渐转为激昂）
（歌队跳舞，搭配源石技艺）
英雄：和煦的阳光下，人们较量武艺而不会危及生命，只为磨练意志与体魄；言辞的交锋不是出于仇恨的谩骂，而是为了探索这片大地最深奥的秘密。
森林不一定是暗藏伏兵的险地，赫里亚的山林在诗篇中有另一种意象；河流不只可以用来冲毁敌军阵地，我们同样可以在其中沐浴高歌。
英雄：蔷薇需要荆棘的保护，美丽的诗篇也需要利剑与坚盾来捍卫。我们也可以用花瓣装点盔甲，将诗句融入战歌。
英雄：看啊，双月已经升至最高处，我相信，此役的胜利也会一如这夜空般澄澈。
（灯光开到最大）
英雄：勇士们，英雄们，最后再打磨一下自己的武器吧。
枯萎的林木会化身养料反哺大地，荒芜的废墟也可以成为重建辉煌的地基。
我们将于今夜夺回我们的信仰，还有米诺斯的历史与未来。
（英雄举起剑，众追随者拿起武器列成一队，歌队唱歌，落幕）
（注意清点道具武器数量，千万不要和真的武器弄混）
——节选自阿克罗蒂村戏剧节的剧目《赫里亚之辉》第三章，帕拉斯在自己饰演的英雄西弗斯台词旁边加上了许多批注。
